why: An INPUT, not a run artifact -- the third file in the family after arch-arms-
sampling.json (E/W/M/H) and arch-hive-sampling.json (B0/B1), and deliberately a
THIRD file rather than a section inside either. Each loader validates over its
own arm order, so P/PR/PH/PN cells in the hive table would be read by nothing
and would put two tasks' hands on one file. examples/arch_policy.py defines no
fallback for any cell here: a missing cell raises ConfigError naming the arm and
the role, asserted structurally over the module's own AST so a default cannot be
reintroduced quietly.
Model identities live here for arch_arms' reason, unchanged: the cortex 'model'
is null on purpose, resolved from the environment or recorded ABSENT -- never
substituted with a predecessor.
NULL DELIBERATELY, matching arch-arms-sampling.json and arch-hive-sampling.json.
The cortex is dialled by arm P and by NO other arm here: it writes the policy
source, exactly once per episode, and then takes no further part. The three
control arms carry no cortex cell at all, which is what makes 'zero authoring
calls' a fact about the configuration rather than a promise about the code.
Serves ESCALATIONS -- the declared checkpoint where a mind intervenes. Dialled
through examples/worker_seam.py on the same path arm B1's scoped calls take,
because an escalation IS a B1 scoped call: a typed question over an enumerated
answer space, authored by the harness, answered advisory. Spec claim c20's
caste vocabulary holds -- the delegation is to a worker-harness the cortex's
own contract shaped, never to a raw mind handed a goal.
Constant in all four arms and NOT dialled by any of them -- recorded and hashed
so a senses difference cannot confound the P-vs-controls contrast invisibly.
What 'thinking: on' puts on the wire, stated rather than assumed. A mode with
no entry here is a config error, never a silent no-op.
Per role per arm, and ONLY for the roles an arm may actually dial. A control
arm has no cortex cell because it makes no authoring call; giving it one would
declare a dial that can never happen.
The cortex cell matches arch-arms-sampling.json and arch-hive-sampling.json
exactly so P is comparable with E/W/M/H/B rather than confounded by sampling.
The worker cell matches arch-hive-sampling.json's B1 worker cell for the same
reason: an escalation and a B1 scoped call are the same call, so they must be
the same dial or the two arms' acceptance figures are not comparable.
authoring_calls is the arm's whole headline claim, held as a number the loader
CHECKS against the arm's structure rather than trusts: arm P is 1 because the
mind writes the policy once, and each control is 0 because its source is
committed in the harness and reviewed. A table that granted a compiled arm two
authoring calls -- a retry -- would be silently measuring a different arm, so
the loader refuses it.
max_escalation_calls bounds the number of escalation calls one episode may
dispatch, in total. It is the step-count bound the structural termination test
reads, and it is clamped before any call is built.
Every arm carries the same escalation budget on purpose: escalation capability
is uniform across the four arms and only the SOURCE differs, which is what
makes the three controls controls rather than different experiments.
The per-arm play table. All four arms are identical here, and that identity IS
the control design: same episode, same jail, same driver, same escalation grain,
same checkpoint role -- the only variable is which source the jail executes.
escalation_role names the mind that answers a declared checkpoint. It is config
rather than a constant because 'which mind intervenes' is a real question the
sweep may vary: the cortex wrote the policy and knows its intent, the worker is
cheaper and is the caste c20 names for scoped typed questions. The reference
cells say worker; task t9's pre-registration is the authority on whether the
sweep varies it.
How many escalated situations ride in one checkpoint call. The same table
arch-hive-sampling.json carries and for the same reason -- scope size is the
independent variable, swept rather than toggled -- narrowed here to the
escalation lane, which is the only lane in this arm that costs a model call at
play time. Task t8 measures the per-call prefill cost before t9 fixes the
sweep's granularity; no grain here is claimed to be the right one.

unit.why: one escalated situation per call -- the finest grain, the most calls

batch4.why: coarse enough that a single refusal costs four answers -- the acceptance risk

batch8.why: the coarse end: one call at measured saturation width, prefill paid once

why: The demo episode's shape. Deterministic and harness-authored: no randomness
generates it, so two arms see byte-identical situations and a difference in
outcome cannot be the episode.
occlusion_every declares how often a situation hides the feature its decision
turns on. Those are the situations where 'I don't know' is the CORRECT return,
and they are what makes escalation quality gradeable at all: the harness knows,
host-side, which situations a policy could not have decided.
seed is carried into the jail payload for the random control. It is here rather
than in code so a re-run is reproducible from a cited file, and it is passed to
EVERY arm's payload so the payload shape does not vary by arm.
The wait deadline for one concurrent escalation batch. Derived, not chosen, and
identical to arch-hive-sampling.json's because it bounds the identical call: a
checkpoint holds ONE turn per call, never a drive, so the bound is the per-turn
bound with no turn-budget multiplier.
256 tokens / 21.5 tok/s = 11.9s; the value below carries a wide margin for
queueing on a --max-num-seqs=2 server rather than sitting near the bound. Task
t2 owns the CI test that recomputes this class of constant; this cell exists so
the escalation deadline is a cited config value when t2 walks it, never a
literal in examples/arch_policy.py.
max_concurrency is measured saturation (docs/live-test-results/worker-
throughput.md), the same 8 arm B1 dials.
PROVISIONAL and named as such -- task t9's pre-registration is the authority on
the sweep, the outcome metric and the stop rule. It lives here as data so t9 can
pin or amend it without a code change.
call_acceptance_refutes_at_rate is the number the frame names by hand: issue #33
measured 74% of workspace-arm calls refused on a shape error. An escalation lane
at that rate is published as REFUTING the delegate-to-authored-artifacts claim,
by name, not smoothed over.
escalation_rate_collapses_at is the OTHER extreme, pre-declared so it cannot be
argued about afterwards: a policy that escalates every decision has collapsed
into the worker arm with extra latency, and is reported as such rather than as a
compiled policy that happened to do well.
policy_acceptance_floor is the compiled artifact's own protocol compliance. It
is the axis that tells a strategically-inert-but-valid policy apart from one
that never returned a legal move, and it is reported separately from both
outcome and escalation acceptance for the same reason those two are separate.
